title: GC 472 taro (NSIC G 10): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: GC 472 taro: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: GC 472 taro is a taro variety. About 8 months to harvest, 9.3 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others.
excerpt: GC 472 is a registered taro variety, also sold or known as NSIC G 10. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2006 as NSIC 2006 Gb 10. It takes about 8 months from planting to harvest, with 9.28 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

items: **Days to harvest:** about 8 months from planting to harvest.
**Yield:** 9.28 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

GC 472 taro takes about 8 months from planting to harvest. That is about the average of the 10 taro varieties with a day count, 8 months. Count the months from planting, and plan the harvest for a dry stretch when you can.

Its average yield of 9.28 t/ha beats the average of its group, 8.82. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting.
The pests and diseases that hit taro fields most often: [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its roots have white flesh and pink purple skin. Dry matter is 42.86 percent. A higher dry matter cooks mealy and gives processors more flour or starch from each tonne. It is recommended for food.
Where and when to plant GC 472 taro
It is recommended for anywhere in the country. Gabi grows in wet lowland or on upland beds. Pick a variety for the land you have, and for the corm, the leaves or both.

items.q: Is NSIC G 10 the same as GC 472?
items.a: Yes. NSIC G 10 is another name for GC 472, registered as NSIC 2006 Gb 10. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 8 months from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 9.28 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
It is recommended for anywhere in the country. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of GC 472?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
